```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(glmnet); library(dplyr); library(tibble)
  library(purrr); library(reactable); library(knitr)
})
```

## What this does

Performance of the GTEx tissue clocks, reported two ways.

In-sample metrics come from the deployed clock evaluated on the GTEx samples it
was fit on. These are read directly from the saved Step 02 predictions and
nothing is refit, so they describe how well the deployed model fits its own
training data. They are optimistic by construction and are reported for
comparability with clock studies that publish training fit.

Nested cross-validation re-runs the full alpha/lambda tuning (Step 02's search)
inside each outer fold, so the reported R2/RMSE/MAE account for hyperparameter
selection, not just fitting. This is the honest generalization estimate and the
one quoted in the main text. It validates the *procedure*; the deployed clock is
still the full-data model from Step 02. Its alpha and lambda are shown for
reference.

Both R2 values are the squared Pearson correlation between predicted and
chronological age, so the two columns are directly comparable. Read-only:
nothing downstream changes.

Two versions of the table are written: the full numeric table at `out_csv`, and
a condensed version alongside it with `_condensed` appended to the file name.

```{r helpers}
# Age-decile-stratified k folds (matches Step 02's stratification).
build_foldid <- function(y, k, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  bin <- dplyr::ntile(y, 10)
  f <- integer(length(y))
  for (b in sort(unique(bin))) {
    idx <- which(bin == b)
    f[idx] <- sample(rep(seq_len(k), length.out = length(idx)))
  }
  f
}

# Nested CV: tune (alpha grid x lambda via inner CV, lambda.1se) inside each
# outer fold, refit on outer-train, predict the held-out outer fold.
nested_oof <- function(x, y, alpha_grid, lambda_grid, outer_k, inner_k, seed) {
  outer_fold <- build_foldid(y, outer_k, seed)
  oof <- rep(NA_real_, length(y))
  for (of in seq_len(outer_k)) {
    tr <- outer_fold != of; te <- outer_fold == of
    x_tr <- x[tr, , drop = FALSE]; y_tr <- y[tr]
    inner_fold <- build_foldid(y_tr, inner_k, seed + of)

    picks <- purrr::map_dfr(alpha_grid, function(a) {
      cv <- cv.glmnet(x_tr, y_tr, alpha = a, foldid = inner_fold,
                      type.measure = "mae", lambda = lambda_grid,
                      standardize = TRUE, intercept = TRUE)
      j <- which(cv$lambda == cv$lambda.1se)
      tibble(alpha = a, lambda = cv$lambda.1se, mae = cv$cvm[j])
    })
    best <- picks[which.min(picks$mae), ]

    fit <- glmnet(x_tr, y_tr, alpha = best$alpha, lambda = best$lambda,
                  standardize = TRUE, intercept = TRUE)
    oof[te] <- as.numeric(predict(fit, newx = x[te, , drop = FALSE], s = best$lambda))
  }
  oof
}
```

```{r core}
process_one <- function(analysis_id) {
  suffix <- paste0("-", params$feature_set)
  adir   <- file.path(params$out_root, analysis_id)
  clock  <- readRDS(file.path(adir, paste0("clock_and_RAA_objects", suffix, ".rds")))
  scores <- readRDS(file.path(adir, paste0("ssgsea_scores_gtex",     suffix, ".rds")))
  meta   <- readRDS(file.path(adir, "sample_metadata.rds"))

  feat        <- clock$feature_names
  alpha_grid  <- as.numeric(clock$tuning$alpha_grid)
  lambda_grid <- as.numeric(clock$tuning$lambda_grid)
  if (length(alpha_grid) == 0) alpha_grid <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)

  # Rebuild the training matrix exactly as Step 02.
  x <- t(scores)[, feat, drop = FALSE]
  y <- meta[rownames(x), "age_years"]
  keep <- is.finite(y)
  x <- x[keep, , drop = FALSE]; y <- as.numeric(y[keep])

  # In-sample: deployed clock on its own training samples, straight from Step 02.
  pred_in <- clock$pred$GTEx
  age_in  <- clock$age$GTEx[names(pred_in)]
  ok_in   <- is.finite(pred_in) & is.finite(age_in)

  # The two R2 columns are only comparable if both are computed over the same
  # GTEx samples; warn rather than stop, since a small difference may be benign.
  if (sum(ok_in) != length(y)) {
    warning(analysis_id, ": in-sample n (", sum(ok_in),
            ") differs from rebuilt training n (", length(y), ").")
  }

  fit_r2   <- cor(pred_in[ok_in], age_in[ok_in])^2                   # squared Pearson r
  fit_rmse <- sqrt(mean((pred_in[ok_in] - age_in[ok_in])^2))
  fit_mae  <- mean(abs(pred_in[ok_in] - age_in[ok_in]))

  oof <- nested_oof(x, y, alpha_grid, lambda_grid,
                    params$outer_k, params$inner_k, params$seed)
  ok  <- is.finite(oof) & is.finite(y)

  cv_r2   <- cor(oof[ok], y[ok])^2                                   # squared Pearson r
  # cv_r2 <- 1 - sum((oof[ok]-y[ok])^2)/sum((y[ok]-mean(y[ok]))^2)   # variance-explained alt.
  cv_rmse <- sqrt(mean((oof[ok] - y[ok])^2))
  cv_mae  <- mean(abs(oof[ok] - y[ok]))

  n_nonzero <- if (!is.null(clock$retained)) nrow(clock$retained)
               else sum(clock$clock_cs$beta != 0, na.rm = TRUE)

  tibble(
    `GTEx tissue`            = sub(".*__", "", analysis_id),
    `n GTEx`                 = length(y),
    `Age median`             = median(y),
    `Age SD`                 = round(sd(y), 2),
    `Age min`                = min(y),
    `Age max`                = max(y),
    `Input pathways`         = length(feat),
    `Nonzero-coef pathways`  = n_nonzero,
    `In-sample R2`           = round(fit_r2, 3),
    `In-sample RMSE`         = round(fit_rmse, 2),
    `In-sample MAE`          = round(fit_mae, 2),
    `Nested-CV R2`           = round(cv_r2, 3),
    `Nested-CV RMSE`         = round(cv_rmse, 2),
    `Nested-CV MAE`          = round(cv_mae, 2),
    `Deployed alpha`         = as.numeric(clock$tuning$best_alpha),
    `Deployed lambda`        = signif(as.numeric(clock$tuning$best_lambda), 4)
  )
}

perf_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(params$analyses, process_one)
```

## Table

```{r table}
knitr::kable(perf_tbl, caption = "GTEx tissue clocks: descriptors, in-sample fit, and nested-CV performance.")
reactable::reactable(perf_tbl, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE, defaultPageSize = 8)
```

```{r save, eval=isTRUE(params$save_outputs)}
dir.create(dirname(params$out_csv), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
readr::write_csv(perf_tbl, params$out_csv)
message("Wrote: ", params$out_csv)
```

## Condensed table for the supplement

The same values with the paired statistics folded into single cells, which
brings the table to eight columns so that it fits a portrait page. Age SD and
both MAE columns are dropped here and remain in the full table above and in the
saved CSV.

```{r table_condensed}
perf_condensed <- perf_tbl %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Tissue                = `GTEx tissue`,
    n                     = `n GTEx`,
    `Age, median (range)` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", `Age median`, `Age min`, `Age max`),
    Pathways              = sprintf("%d of %d", as.integer(`Nonzero-coef pathways`),
                                                as.integer(`Input pathways`)),
    `In-sample R2 (RMSE)` = sprintf("%.3f (%.1f)", `In-sample R2`, `In-sample RMSE`),
    `Nested-CV R2 (RMSE)` = sprintf("%.3f (%.1f)", `Nested-CV R2`, `Nested-CV RMSE`),
    alpha                 = `Deployed alpha`,
    lambda                = `Deployed lambda`
  )

knitr::kable(
  perf_condensed,
  caption = paste0(
    "GTEx tissue clocks, condensed for typesetting. R2 is the squared Pearson ",
    "correlation between predicted and chronological age; RMSE is in years. ",
    "In-sample values come from the deployed clock evaluated on its own ",
    "training samples and are optimistic by construction."
  )
)
```

```{r save_condensed, eval=isTRUE(params$save_outputs)}
out_csv_condensed <- sub("\\.csv$", "_condensed.csv", params$out_csv)

dir.create(dirname(out_csv_condensed), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
readr::write_csv(perf_condensed, out_csv_condensed)
message("Wrote: ", out_csv_condensed)
```
